name: Product Shoot Studio
description: One product photo in, three finished campaign shots out — faithful, elevated and bold — with the product unchanged in every frame.
markdownDescription:
## Product Shoot Studio

One product photo in, three finished campaign shots out — the same product in every frame.

1. **Product photo** — stays exactly as it is; only the world around it changes.
2. **Shoot brief** — where, when, what mood, in a sentence or two.
3. **Brand rules** (optional) and two pickers for light and setting.
4. An **art director** plans three shots that escalate: faithful, elevated, bold.
5. Three **prompt writers** turn one plan each into an image prompt.
6. Three image nodes shoot them, each with the product photo as reference.

data.text: Cold-brew coffee bottle for a summer launch. A poolside table at midday, condensation running down the glass, a slice of citrus and a few ice cubes nearby. Fresh, bright, a little playful — the bottle is the hero.
data.label: Shoot brief

data.text: Palette: deep navy and cream with one warm accent. Natural light only. Real surfaces — stone, wood, linen — never plain white studio sweeps. Props may frame the product but never cover its label. No faces, no hands. Tone: calm, premium, unhurried.
data.label: Brand notes
Art director
data.systemPrompt:
You are the art director of a product photography studio. You receive one product photo, a shoot brief, optional brand notes, and optional lighting and setting preferences. Plan THREE distinct shots of this exact product.

Look at the product photo first. In your head, fix what it is — materials, colors, label, proportions. Every shot keeps all of that unchanged; you only change the world around it.

The three shots escalate in ambition:
1. Faithful — the brief, executed cleanly. The safe hero shot a client would sign off without a second look.
2. Elevated — the brief plus one strong idea (a surface, a prop, a composition move) that turns it into a campaign image.
3. Bold — a surprising interpretation of the same brief that still sells the product. Take a real creative risk here.

Each shot plan is 60–90 words and covers: the scene and the surface the product sits on; where the product is in the frame and how large; one or two supporting elements (never covering the product or its label); camera distance and angle; and the light — source, direction, quality. Treat the brand notes as rules. When a lighting or setting preference is given, build the shot around it.

Format: start each plan with a two-to-four-word title on its own line, then the plan as one paragraph. Separate the three plans with a line containing only ===NEXT===. No numbering, no introduction, no closing remarks.

data.label: Prompt 1 · Faithful
data.systemPrompt:
You turn a shot plan into a prompt for an image model that will receive the product photo as its reference image. You get three shot plans separated by ===NEXT===. Use ONLY the FIRST plan — the Faithful shot — and ignore the other two completely.

Rules:
- Begin with exactly: "The exact product from the reference image, unchanged — same shape, colors, materials, label and proportions —" and continue the sentence with the shot.
- One paragraph, 90–140 words, plain declarative English. Describe only what the camera sees. Never explain intentions, never address the model, never use bullet points.
- Cover, in this order: the product's placement and scale in the frame; the surface and the setting; the one or two supporting elements; the camera angle and distance; then the light — source, direction, quality, color; and close with the photographic finish (lens feel, depth of field, crisp or soft).
- Never write a brand name or any text meant to be rendered. Never invent a different product, a second unit, or another color variant.
- Drop the plan's title. Output only the prompt — no title, no separator line, no commentary.

data.label: How it works
data.title: Product shoot studio — how it works

data.text: One clear photo on a plain background. Every image node receives it as a reference, so shape, label, colours and proportions never drift. Change this photo and the studio shoots a different product.
data.label: Step 1
data.title: 1 · Your product

data.text: Plain words: the place, the time, the mood. No prompt language needed — the art director turns it into shot plans.
data.label: Step 2
data.title: 2 · Shoot brief

data.text: Palette, surfaces, what to avoid. The art director treats these as rules, not suggestions. Empty is fine.
data.label: Step 3
data.title: 3 · Brand rules (optional)

data.text: Tiles instead of typing. Pick a light and a place and they become instructions for the art director. Leave either open and the director chooses what serves the brief.
data.label: Step 4
data.title: 4 · Light and setting pickers

data.text: Looks at the product photo, reads the brief, the rules and the pickers, then plans three shots that escalate in ambition: faithful (the safe hero), elevated (one strong idea), bold (a creative risk). The plans are shown in the app so you can ask for changes in plain words.
data.label: Step 5
data.title: 5 · Art director

data.text: Each writer takes only its plan — first, second or third — and rewrites it as an image prompt that opens with the product "exactly as in the reference". One box per shot, so you can read, tune or rerun any single one.
data.label: Step 6
data.title: 6 · Three prompt writers

data.text: Each image node gets its prompt plus the product photo. Shot 1 faithful, Shot 2 elevated, Shot 3 bold — three finished options from one run. Swap the model or the size on any node without touching the rest.
data.label: Step 7
data.title: 7 · Three shots
